h1: What to Expect During a Pest Inspection
dek: Learn what happens during a professional pest inspection, from arrival to report to quote, so you walk in knowing exactly what's next.
author: Nick Davies
answer: A professional pest inspection usually takes 30 to 90 minutes. The inspector walks your property inside and out, checking common trouble spots like kitchens, bathrooms, attics, basements, and the foundation for live pests, droppings, damage, and moisture problems. You'll get a written report of what they found and a treatment quote before they leave — no pressure to decide on the spot.

jsonld.name: What Happens During a Pest Inspection

step.name: Arrival and walkthrough discussion
step.text: The inspector arrives, asks what pest activity you've noticed, and explains the areas they plan to check.

step.name: Interior inspection
step.text: The inspector checks kitchens, bathrooms, basements or crawlspaces, and attics for signs of pests, droppings, damage, and moisture.

step.name: Exterior inspection
step.text: The inspector examines the foundation, siding, eaves, and yard perimeter for entry points and conducive conditions.

step.name: Report review
step.text: The inspector shares a written report identifying findings, evidence, and conducive conditions, often with photos.

step.name: Quote and next steps
step.text: You receive a written treatment quote with options and no obligation to decide immediately.

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the company. Many offer a free general inspection as a way to quote treatment work. Specialized inspections — like a termite letter needed for a home sale — more often carry a fee. If you don't have an urgent problem, it's worth calling around, since a free inspection is a low-risk way to get a professional opinion.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to be home during the inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most cases. The inspector will need access to interior areas like the kitchen, bathrooms, attic, and crawlspace, and it helps to be there to answer questions and point out problem areas.

mainEntity.name: Will the inspector treat the pest problem the same day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, but not always. Many companies separate inspection and treatment into two visits, especially for larger jobs like termite treatment, while simpler issues may be treated the same day.

mainEntity.name: What if the inspector finds termites?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll get a detailed report on the extent of damage and a treatment plan, which may involve a specialized termite company. Termite treatment often requires follow-up visits to confirm the colony is eliminated.

mainEntity.name: How often should I schedule a pest inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most homes, an annual inspection is a reasonable baseline, with more frequent visits in high-risk termite areas or homes that have had recurring problems.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I decide not to move forward with treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing. A legitimate company will give you the report and quote and let you decide on your own timeline, with no pressure to commit on the spot.
